text:
1) I had no maternity leave, but it was because I wasn’t eligible. Usually the payment is based on documentation transfer from hospital to Bituach Leumi. She will need to pick all documents from hospital abroad or documentation written and given by pediatrician and doula if she is going to give birth at home, having them translated and notarized and communicate it with Bituach Leumi and Misrad Hapnim. We needed all these documents for Misrad Hapnim anyway to be able to register child as Israeli citizen.

2) we didnt register our child on embassy because they told us it will take minimum 6 months to register baby as israeli citizen, give passport and TZ and health insurance. Instead, we flew baby on tourist visa to Israel and registered her ourselves on MH which took less than one month (longest waiting was for translation and notarization of all documents, MH took one day). We needed all documents- papers about pregnancy (but these I had from Israel), documentation about giving birth and about the release of mother and the newborn from hospital (everywhere needed to be written the name of the baby and date of birth, so we needed to name her on the very first day and couldn’t wait longer which someones prefers to perform naming ceremony only few days later, so this wasn’t possible). We also brought documentation about first baby health checks performed by pediatrician. Of course birth certificate was needed too and in our case also declaration of signing my spouse as the father (we are not married). We apostilled everything what needed to be apostilled and after we arrived to Israel, we translated and notarized everything. 

3)I needed to fly abroad when I was 36 weeks pregnant (latest when I could board the plane) and came back 3 months after giving birth. I would fly already 10 weeks after giving birth right away after first vaccination doses, but I had some complications after birth and my medical condition didn’t allow it.

Yes, that year I was 4 months straight out of the country, but MH didn’t make us trouble.
